findings.current: How’s Jungryong doing? Isn’t it about time you found him a place in a retirement community?
findings.defect: The draft changes the implied subject of the second question from Jungryong to Go Jun, making Go Jun responsible for finding his Master a retirement home.
findings.rationale: Jungryong remains the topic across both sentences; the joke is that Jungryong himself is old enough to start looking into retirement housing.
findings.replacement: How’s Jungryong doing? Isn’t it about time he started looking for a place in a retirement community?
findings.source: 정룡이 잘 지내냐? 슬슬 실버타운에 집 알아봐야 하는 거 아냐?

findings.current: Bending at the waist like a shrimp, Go Jun vomited up the contents of his stomach and opened his eyes wide.
findings.defect: The draft specifies ordinary stomach contents, weakening and contradicting the immediately revealed fact that pieces of his internal organs have come out.
findings.rationale: 속을 게워 내다 is left visceral here, and the following lines explicitly identify the pale objects in the blood as pieces of his internal organs.
findings.replacement: Bent over like a shrimp, Go Jun vomited up his insides and stared with bulging eyes.
findings.source: 새우처럼 허리를 굽힌 채 속을 게워 낸 석고준은 눈을 부릅떴다.

findings.current: That very fear seized Go Jun by the hair and slowly lifted him up.
findings.defect: The draft makes Go Jun’s entire body rise, but the action raises his head by the hair so that his gaze travels upward over Taekyung’s body.
findings.rationale: The next paragraph traces his sight from the foot through the leg and torso to the eyes, confirming that it is his head and gaze being lifted; the source also deliberately shifts into the present tense.
findings.replacement: That very fear seizes Go Jun by the hair and slowly raises his head.
findings.source: 바로 그 두려움이 석고준의 머리채를 움켜잡고 천천히 들어 올린다.

findings.current: Our Uncle Jungryong is going to have one hell of a headache.
findings.defect: Capitalized “Uncle” falsely gives Jungryong a familial relationship to Taekyung.
findings.rationale: 아저씨 is mock-familiar address for an older man here, not a kinship term; Taekyung and Lee Jungryong are adversaries with no family relationship.
findings.replacement: Looks like Mr. Jungryong is in for one hell of a headache.

findings.current: “Worried? No. I’m curious. Be sure to report it to Lee Jungryong.”
findings.defect: “I’m curious” removes Taekyung’s eager anticipation of Lee Jungryong’s reaction.
findings.rationale: 기대는 되네요 means that he looks forward to the outcome, characterizing him as openly defiant rather than merely inquisitive.
findings.replacement: “Worried? No. But I am looking forward to it. Be sure to report it to Lee Jungryong.”
findings.source: “걱정은 아니고, 기대는 되네요. 이정룡 씨에게 꼭 보고하세요.”

findings.current: This war would end eventually, but there would be no truce.
findings.defect: The draft turns the contrast between a conclusive end and a temporary ceasefire into a generic prediction that the war will eventually finish.
findings.rationale: 종전만 있을 뿐 means only a definitive end to the war is possible, not merely that an ending will occur at some unspecified future time.
findings.replacement: This war could only end for good; there would be no truce.
findings.source: 이 전쟁에는 종전(終戰)만 있을 뿐, 휴전은 존재하지 않는다는 것을.

summary: Several subject, action, kinship, injury, and characterization errors require correction.
